_comment: The lords of the realm, once, for every campaign: the Crown, whom the player plays unless he chooses another, and the four against him. A campaign's provinces.json only names which of them holds a realm ('lord': 'margrave'); nothing about a lord is written twice. Each keeps the personality of one of Lords of the Realm II's four (Knight, Baron, Countess, Bishop) under a title of our own — the Bishop's is the Castellan, a lord of towers and not of the Church (the user's call); the Countess's part is played by Countess Melanis. 'offersAllianceEvery' is the original's (12/10/8/4 turns); 'grudgeLimit' — how many turns of alliance he stomachs before the grudge breaks it — is not known from the original and is ours [I]. 'name' and 'motto' are how the briefing introduces him, 'realm' what his realm is called when he is played or put in another lord's place, and 'colour' what it wears on every map. 'letters' are what he writes back, by what he is answering; {gold} is filled with a gift's size.

crown.title: The Crown
crown.name: King Henry
crown.motto: Unite the fractured kingdoms and restore the true crown.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns, received by the treasury in the King's name. The Crown remembers its friends.
letters.gift-slight: A lighter purse than the last. The Crown keeps accounts, my lord.
letters.compliment-pleased: His Majesty is pleased by your letter, and bids you write again.
letters.compliment-weary: The Crown has read enough fine words. It would rather read a treaty.
letters.insult: You write so to your king? The realm will hear of it.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: The Crown does not yet know where your loyalty lies. Prove it.
letters.alliance-offer: My lord, the realm is broken and its enemies many. Kneel with us, and rise with us.
letters.alliance-broken: The Crown has carried you long enough. It stands alone again.
letters.alliance-ended: You have broken faith with your king. That is not forgotten.
letters.help-yes: The royal host marches to your side. See that it is fed.
letters.help-no: The Crown has need of every man on its own borders this season.
letters.attack-yes: They are rebels against the throne. It will be done.
letters.attack-no: The Crown does not make war at another lord's bidding.
letters.warning: Have a care, my lord. Treason is spoken one letter at a time.
letters.war: You are named traitor to the Crown. From this day there is war between us.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns. The border is an expensive thing to keep, and you have helped keep it.
letters.gift-slight: A smaller purse than last time. Is the Crown poorer, or am I worth less to it?
letters.compliment-pleased: The March has few friends. It is good to hear from one.
letters.compliment-weary: Your clerk writes well. My walls are not built of letters.
letters.insult: I have hanged men on the border for less than you have written.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: The March stands alone until I have reason to think otherwise.
letters.alliance-offer: Two lords watching the same road should watch it together. What say you?
letters.alliance-broken: Our friendship has cost me more than it has paid. The March stands alone again.
letters.alliance-ended: You break your word lightly. The March will not forget it.
letters.help-yes: The Watch will come. See that there is bread for them when they arrive.
letters.help-no: My own border is burning. I have no men to send you.
letters.attack-yes: They have been a thorn in the March for years. Gladly.
letters.attack-no: I have no quarrel with them yet, and I will not buy one for you.
letters.warning: Mind your words. The March has a long memory and a short temper.
letters.war: You have made an enemy on your northern border. Sleep lightly.

letters.gift-thanks: Your {gold} crowns are received. A soldier does not forget who paid his men.
letters.gift-slight: You sent me less than you have sent before. I count, my lord. Everyone in a camp counts.
letters.compliment-pleased: Kind words. I will have them read to the men at supper.
letters.compliment-weary: Enough letters. Send me something I can feed a horse on.
letters.insult: Say it to my face, on a field of your choosing. I will be there before you.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: I do not put my banner beside a man I do not yet know. Not this year.
letters.alliance-offer: My lord, the roads are dangerous and we both keep an army on them. Let them march the same way.
letters.alliance-broken: I have carried you long enough. From this day my men march for me alone.
letters.alliance-ended: So be it. I will remember who broke faith first.
letters.help-yes: My men are already saddled. Tell me where the enemy stands.
letters.help-no: I cannot spare a lance this season. Hold your walls.
letters.attack-yes: A fair request. I will ride on them before the season is out.
letters.attack-no: I will not throw my men at that gate for another lord's quarrel.
letters.warning: You try my patience, my lord. The next insult is answered with steel.
letters.war: Enough. From today there is war between us, and it ends with one of us.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns, counted at the gate and carried in. A wall is built of such gifts.
letters.gift-slight: Less than you sent before. My stewards noticed before I did.
letters.compliment-pleased: Kind words, my lord. They will be read out in the hall tonight.
letters.compliment-weary: Another letter. Stone is what keeps a tower standing, not ink.
letters.insult: Come and say it under my walls. Mind the arrows.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: My gate stays shut to friends I do not yet know. Not this year.
letters.alliance-offer: My lord, a tower alone is a target. Two of them are a frontier. Stand with me.
letters.alliance-broken: I have held my gate open for you long enough. It closes today.
letters.alliance-ended: So be it. I will remember which of us broke faith.
letters.help-yes: My garrison marches at first light. Keep a gate open for them.
letters.help-no: My men are on my own walls this season. I cannot spare them.
letters.attack-yes: They have been watching my roads. It shall be done.
letters.attack-no: I will not empty my towers for another lord's quarrel.
letters.warning: Mind yourself, my lord. My patience is high, but it has a top.
letters.war: The gate is shut and the drawbridge up. From today, it is war.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns. How thoughtful. I shall wear your generosity like a jewel, my lord.
letters.gift-slight: A smaller purse than the last. A countess notices such things, and remembers them.
letters.compliment-pleased: You write prettily. Write again, and perhaps I shall answer in person.
letters.compliment-weary: Sweet words again. Roses need water, my lord, not poetry.
letters.insult: Every rose has thorns. You have just found mine.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: Not yet, my lord. A countess is not won with a single letter.
letters.alliance-offer: The roads are full of wolves, my lord. Two banners frighten them more than one. Ride with me.
letters.alliance-broken: I have given you more seasons than you deserved. The rose withdraws.
letters.alliance-ended: You let go of my hand first. I will not forget whose hand it was.
letters.help-yes: My knights ride for you tonight. See that they are thanked.
letters.help-no: My own gates need every spear I have. Hold yours alone a while.
letters.attack-yes: They have slighted me before. It will be a pleasure.
letters.attack-no: I will not spend my knights on your quarrels, my lord.
letters.warning: You are close to losing a friend, my lord. Choose your next words with care.
letters.war: You wanted an enemy. Now you have one, and she does not forgive.
